nodes.name: Drop-casting and annealing RuO₂
nodes.procedure: 35 μl of aqueous RuCl₃ solution (20 mmol l⁻¹) drop-cast onto FTO substrate (1×1 cm²) heated at 70°C on hot plate. After solution dried, FTO substrate coated with RuCl₃ moved to muffle furnace and annealed at 500°C for 2 h.

unit_operations.name: Annealing
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: the FTO substrate coated with RuCl₃ was moved into a muffle furnace and annealed at 500°C for 2 h

nodes.source_text: Typically, RuO₂ was synthesized by drop-casting 35 μl of aqueous RuCl₃ solution (20 mmol l⁻¹) onto fluorine-doped tin oxide (FTO) substrate with an area of 1×1 cm² heated at 70°C... annealed at 500°C for 2 h.

nodes.name: Modified RuO₂ with NaCl
nodes.procedure: Same concentration of RuCl₃ was used as standard RuO₂ synthesis, but NaCl was added with molar ratio Ru:Na = 1:3. 35 μl solution drop-cast onto FTO heated at 70°C, dried, then annealed at 500°C for 2 h.
nodes.source_text: For the modified RuO₂ with N₂Φ⁺ (denoted as m-RuO₂), the same concentration of RuCl₃ was used, but a certain amount of NaCl was added... molar ratio of Ru:Na = 1:3.

nodes.name: Low-temperature RuO₂
nodes.procedure: Same procedure as standard RuO₂ but annealed at 300°C instead of 500°C.
nodes.source_text: RuO₂ sample with lower crystallinity and more defects was also synthesized at 300°C, denoted as RuO₂(300°C).

nodes.name: Co-doped RuO₂
nodes.procedure: Same concentration of RuCl₃ with Co precursor at molar ratio Ru:Co = 20:1. Drop-cast 35 μl onto FTO at 70°C, dried, annealed at 500°C for 2 h.
nodes.source_text: Co-doped RuO₂ (denoted as Co-RuO₂) was also synthesized using the same concentration of RuCl₃ and a molar ratio of Ru:Co = 20:1.

nodes.name: Au sputtering on RuO₂
nodes.procedure: Au deposited onto RuO₂ using magnetic sputtering at 100°C for 1 min.
nodes.source_text: Au was deposited onto RuO₂ to yield Au/RuO₂ using magnetic sputtering (temperature was set at 100°C for 1 min).

nodes.name: IrO₂ synthesis
nodes.procedure: IrO₂, m-IrO₂ and Co-IrO₂ synthesized similarly to Ru oxides but RuCl₃ replaced by 20 mmol l⁻¹ IrCl₃ aqueous solution (35 μl drop-cast, 70°C drying, 500°C annealing 2 h).
nodes.source_text: For the Ir oxide-based catalysts (IrO₂, m·IrO₂ and Co·IrO₂), the synthesis conditions were similar, but RuCl₃ was replaced by IrCl₃.

nodes.name: PLD oxide synthesis
nodes.procedure: TiO₂, Co₃O₄, WO₃ and SrIrO₃ synthesized on FTO using pulsed laser deposition (PLD). Detailed parameter settings in Supplementary Table 1.
nodes.source_text: These oxides were synthesized on FTO using pulsed laser deposition (PLD).

nodes.name: Electrochemical deposition of metal hydroxides
nodes.procedure: Co, CoFe (10 at.% Fe), and CoNi (25 at.% Ni) hydroxides synthesized by electrochemical deposition following procedure from recent work ref 55, with modified precursor solutions. Ni and NiFe (10 at.% Fe) hydroxides synthesized by anodic electrochemical deposition per Trotochaud et al. ref 56.
nodes.source_text: The metal hydroxides... were synthesized by electrochemical deposition.

nodes.characterization_summary: STEM images show crystalline RuO2 with well-defined structure and m-RuO2 with defects and local lattice distortion highlighted by red circles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: STEM images of crystalline ${ \mathrm { R u O } } _ { 2 }$ (a) and $m { \cdot } \mathrm { R u O } _ { 2 }$ (b). The defects in $m { \cdot } \mathrm { R u O } _ { 2 }$ are highlighted by the red circles.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge XAS shows m-RuO2 exhibits slightly lower Ru oxidation state and shorter Ru–O bond lengths compared with RuO2, consistent with X-ray total scattering.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The changes in local bonding structure of these catalysts were further confirmed by X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) characterization. $m { \cdot } \mathrm { R u O } _ { 2 }$ exhibits a slightly lower Ru oxidation state (Fig. 4e), and shorter Ru–O bond lengths (Fig. 4f) compared with ${ \mathrm { R u O } } _ { 2 }$ , consistent with the X-ray total scattering results (Supplementary Fig. 45).

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman shows RuO2 stable with no bulk structure change but surface rearrangement indicated by peak shift; m-RuO2 shows blue shift consistent with shorter Ru–O bonds.
nodes.evidence_snippet: in situ Raman spectroscopy (Fig. 4g,h and Supplementary Figs. 50–52) reveals that ${ \mathrm { R u O } } _ { 2 }$ is stable with no notable bulk structure change in both acidic H and D electrolytes, but surface rearrangement, as indicated by a peak shift, occurs as soon as contact with the electrolyte.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ FT-IR shows evolution of oxide and superoxide species at 1.0–1.8 V vs RHE/RDE; O–D vibration peak red-shifted compared to O–H; three peaks at 1000-1250 cm⁻¹ attributed to oxide/superoxide species.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In situ Fourier transform infrared (FT-IR) spectroscopy (Fig. 4i and Supplementary Figs. 53 and 54) further reveals that H/D isotope substitution affects the adsorbed species at the electrocatalyst–electrolyte interface: the O–D vibration peak is red-shifted compared with the O–H peak.
X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) was performed on a Thermo Scientific K-Alpha XPS system with an Al Kα X-ray source.
